ideas: Global brands and media spreading everywhere
Young people choosing foreign trends over traditions
Local cultures adapting and mixing, not disappearing

phrases.meaning: sense of belonging to a culture
restaurant brands found in many places
being forced or pushed to change

model: I'd say globalisation is changing local cultures rather than erasing them. While it's true that some traditions are under pressure, I don't think most of them will die out. You can see global influence everywhere, of course. Fast-food chains have been opened in almost every Vietnamese city, and Korean dramas are watched by millions of teenagers here. Some traditional crafts and dialects are definitely disappearing, and that's a real loss. However, local cultures tend to adapt. What often emerges is a blend of old and new. For example, my cousin runs a small café in Hue, and although it looks very modern, the drinks are made with traditional recipes and served in local pottery. It's actually become popular with tourists precisely because it feels Vietnamese. Social media also helps, since small artists can now reach a global audience. So even though globalisation brings a lot of foreign influence, I think people generally hold on to their cultural identity, especially through food, family and festivals.
